title.narrative: Supporting Livelihood Restoration in Agri-fishing Communities Affected by Chain of Tropical Cyclones

description.narrative: The Philippines has faced six devastating cyclones (Trami, Kong-rey, Yinxing, Toraji, Usagi and Man-yi) during October–November 2024, striking the country in rapid succession, affecting over 13 million people across 17 regions. Most of the affected provinces and municipalities are rural areas, where the livelihoods of millions of people depend on farming, fishing and livestock-keeping. Key agricultural commodities, including rice, corn, abaca and coconut, have sustained extensive damage. Successive cyclones have disrupted critical stages of rice and corn cropping, including the October–November harvest season and the planting season starting in November, while also impacting the cultivation of perennial crops. This crisis is further compounded for farming households, who were only beginning to recover from the impacts of El Niño earlier in the year. Among the severely affected provinces are Cagayan and Isabela in region 2 and Catandaunes in region 5. In the rapid needs assessment conducted, local government and communities are citing that livelihood restoration and efforts on supporting them to get back on their feet and rebuild their livelihood is among the top priority and concern of the affected population. This is among the top three needs that the communities wanted to address. In this regard, FAO is answering to the call by implementing response effort that will support livelihood restoration in the affected farming and fishing communities. As such, FAO will be implementing Cash for Livelihood and Cash for Work interventions. The UCT for Emergency Livelihoods offers farmers flexibility to procure essential livelihood assets or inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and other farm-related expenses, addressing immediate recovery needs. This amount is carefully determined to align with the full allocation under the livelihood sector for a three-month period. It reflects the estimated financial needs for essential livelihood activities and support during this time, considering the local context and the economic conditions in which the beneficiaries are operating.Meanwhile, the CCT through cash-for-work activity provides immediate income support by engaging beneficiaries in recovery and rehabilitation activities, such as agricultural restoration or community-based projects. The wage rates are in alignment with the regional minimum daily wage standards, ensuring that the compensation is fair and reflective of local economic conditions. The cash transfer will be provided as a one-off payment upon the successful completion of the required tasks, ensuring that beneficiaries are compensated for their efforts and contributions to the project. The estimated number of workdays is set at 15 days, allowing beneficiaries sufficient time to complete the assigned activities while ensuring that the support provided is both meaningful and adequate to assist in their livelihood recovery. While working on these cash transfer modalities, FAO along with its partners will also conduct capacity building especially on climate smart agriculture and promotion of anticipatory measures which will be done closely with local government units, concern departments and local organization to implement these interventions. In addition to the rapid response activities, this project will also cover the implementation of preparedness activities for CERF AA 2025 implementation which will be under the requested no-cost extension.
